t: You're on High Holborn, a busy street in central London that forms part of the A40 road to Fishguard. Its western stretch, as far as Drury Lane, used to be called Broad Street. Several people have a link to it. Henry Vincent, a Chartist leader and brilliant public speaker who later campaigned against slavery, was born here. So was Harry Randall, a comic actor of music halls and pantomime. The mathematician and theologian John Craig died here, as did Richard Leveridge, a bass singer and composer of popular songs.
